plato.name: Plato of Athens
plato.role: Founder of the Academy & Architect of Mathematical Philosophy
plato.bio: Founded the Athenian Academy (c. 387 BC), elevating pure arithmetic, plane geometry, solid geometry, mathematical astronomy, and harmonics into the indispensable propaedeutic to dialectic and catalyzing the research of Theaetetus and Eudoxus.

socrates.name: Socrates of Athens
socrates.role: Dialectical Interlocutor in Meno, Theaetetus, Republic & Philebus
socrates.bio: Guides Meno's attendant through the diagonal doubling proof, frames Theaetetus's classification of powers, expounds the Divided Line and Quadrivium, and analyzes Limit (peras) and pure geometric beauty in the Philebus.

meno.name: Meno of Pharsalus
meno.role: Thessalian Aristocrat & Interlocutor of the Meno
meno.bio: Raises the celebrated paradox of inquiry (Meno 80d), prompting Socrates' geometric demonstration of recollection on his Greek-speaking household attendant and the method of inquiry from hypothesis.

theodorus.name: Theodorus of Cyrene
theodorus.role: Pythagorean Geometer & Teacher of Plato and Theaetetus
theodorus.bio: Proved case-by-case via diagrams that the sides of squares of 3, 5, ..., 17 square feet are incommensurable in length with the 1-foot unit (Theaetetus 147d).

theaetetus.name: Theaetetus of Athens
theaetetus.role: Academic Geometer of Irrational Powers & the Five Regular Solids
theaetetus.bio: Generalized Theodorus's surds into the universal classification of lengths (mēkē) and powers (dynameis), founded the theory of medial/binomial/apotome irrationals (Euclid Book X), and first constructed all five regular polyhedra (Euclid Book XIII).

glaucon.name: Glaucon of Athens
glaucon.role: Elder Brother of Plato & Interlocutor of Republic Books VI–VII
glaucon.bio: Converse partner with Socrates throughout the Divided Line (509d–511e) and the mathematical curriculum of the Quadrivium (525a–534e).

timaeus.name: Timaeus of Locri
timaeus.role: Italic Pythagorean Astronomer-Statesman & Speaker of the Timaeus
timaeus.bio: Expounds the geometric proportion binding the four elements, the harmonic division of the World-Soul (31b–36d), and the reconstruction of physical bodies from elementary isosceles and scalene right triangles (53c–56c).

parmenides.name: Parmenides of Elea
parmenides.role: Founder of Eleatic Ontology & Speaker of the Eight Hypotheses
parmenides.bio: Conducts the dialectical exercise of Parmenides 137c–166c, articulating the foundational definitions of equidistant roundness and optical straightness (137e, 145b).

protarchus.name: Protarchus of Athens
protarchus.bio: Examines with Socrates the fourfold ontology of Limit, Unlimited, Mixture, and Cause (16c–26d) and the pure beauty of compass-and-straightedge forms (51b–52c).

athenian-stranger.name: The Athenian Stranger
athenian-stranger.bio: Denounces Greek pedagogical ignorance of three-dimensional incommensurability in Laws VII (817e–820d) before Clinias of Crete and Megillus of Sparta.

pythagoras.name: Pythagoras & the Italic Pythagoreans
pythagoras.role: Pioneers of Harmonic Ratios, Figurate Numbers & Application of Areas
pythagoras.bio: Discovered the diatonic ratios (2:1, 3:2, 4:3, 9:8, 256:243), the application of areas, and quadratic incommensurability; commended in Republic VII 530d as treating astronomy and harmonics as sister sciences.

archytas.name: Archytas of Tarentum
archytas.role: Pythagorean Geometer, Theorist of the Three Means & Friend of Plato
archytas.bio: Defined the arithmetic, geometric, and harmonic means in music (DK 47 B2), proved no superparticular ratio (n+1):n admits a rational mean proportional, and solved the doubling of the cube in three dimensions by intersecting a cylinder, torus, and cone.

eudoxus.name: Eudoxus of Cnidus
eudoxus.role: Academic Geometer of General Proportion & Method of Exhaustion
eudoxus.bio: Answered Plato's challenges with the general theory of proportion valid for commensurable and incommensurable magnitudes alike (Euclid Book V) and rigorous stereometric volume theorems (Euclid Book XII).

aristotle.name: Aristotle of Stagira
aristotle.role: Student of Plato & Author of the Analytics, Physics, De Caelo & Metaphysics
aristotle.bio: Preserves vital testimony on Plato's mathematical intermediates (ta mathēmatika), resolves Meno's paradox in Posterior Analytics I.1, and critiques the Timaeus planar-triangle physics in De Caelo III.7–8.

euclid.name: Euclid of Alexandria
euclid.role: Author of the Thirteen Books of Elements
euclid.bio: Systematized the geometric heritage of Plato's Academy, culminating in Book X (Theaetetus's irrationals) and Book XIII (construction and uniqueness of the five Platonic cosmic polyhedra, praised by Proclus as the telos of the Elements).

crantor.name: Crantor of Soli
crantor.role: Old Academic First Exegete of Plato's Timaeus
crantor.bio: Introduced the lambda (Λ) arrangement of the doubles (1, 2, 4, 8) and triples (1, 3, 9, 27) and the least integer base 384 clearing all fractions of the 34-term World-Soul diatonic scale.

proclus.name: Proclus Diadochus
proclus.role: Neoplatonic Diadochus & Commentator on Euclid I and Plato's Timaeus
proclus.bio: Wove Philebus's Limit/Unlimited, Republic's Divided Line (dianoia), Meno's anamnesis, and Timaeus's polyhedra into the Prologue of his Commentary on the First Book of Euclid's Elements.

thomas-aquinas.name: St. Thomas Aquinas
thomas-aquinas.role: Scholastic Doctor of Mathematical Abstraction & Judgment
thomas-aquinas.bio: Synthesized Platonic-Aristotelian mathematical epistemology through abstraction in intelligible matter and resolution to imagination (resolutio ad imaginationem).

pacioli.name: Fra Luca Pacioli
pacioli.role: Renaissance Mathematician & Author of De Divina Proportione (1509)
pacioli.bio: Celebrated Timaeus 53c–56c across nine chapters of De Divina Proportione, pairing Leonardo da Vinci's skeletal polyhedral plates with Euclid Book XIII and the golden ratio.

burnet.name: John Burnet
burnet.role: Editor of the Oxford Classical Text Platonis Opera (1900–1907)
burnet.bio: Scottish classicist at St Andrews whose five-volume Clarendon Press critical edition established the authoritative modern Greek text and Stephanus apparatus of Plato.

jowett.name: Benjamin Jowett
jowett.role: Master of Balliol College, Oxford & Translator of The Dialogues of Plato
jowett.bio: Produced the monumental five-volume English translation of Plato (3rd revised edition, 1892), staged in the English track of this Codex alongside corrective mathematical philology notes.

heath.name: Sir Thomas Little Heath
heath.role: Historian of Greek Mathematics & Editor of Euclid's Elements
heath.bio: Author of A History of Greek Mathematics (1921) and The Thirteen Books of Euclid's Elements (1926), reconstructing Meno 86e–87b, Theodorus's proofs, and Timaeus's astronomy.

hoenen.name: Fr. Petrus H. J. Hoenen, S.J.
hoenen.role: Gregorian University Philosopher of Science & Author of De Noetica Geometriae (1952)
hoenen.bio: Analyzed Meno 82b–85b and Republic VI–VII as perennial witnesses to intellectual insight into geometric necessity within the singular diagram.
